about.summary: Houses and halls built to look like ancient Greek temples, with columns and a triangle on top.
about.compare: Columns and triangle gables, from about 1820

cues.explain: A porch of tall columns across the front, like a temple's.
A low triangular pediment crowns the porch or the front gable.
A broad band runs along the top of the walls, under the roof.
Windows and door line up evenly, often five across the front.

plate.caption: The Clarke House, Chicago's oldest building, photographed in 1856.
plate.credit: Historic American Buildings Survey, Library of Congress (copy of an 1856 photograph)
